request.state: The Can project currently specifies a company SaaS language through .can contracts and manually authored JS targets; its compiler, attachment service and chatbot connection code are absent. Its priorities combine easy adoption with few authored tokens, without weakening evidence or access. Under DESIGN §8 an upload starts with authorization, carries real bounded content, becomes an immutable finalized object, and expires if left unattached. A file argument denotes a completed opaque reference: newly finalized content is scoped to the active app/team/person, and an already-attached object is reusable only when readable by that person. Knowing its identifier supplies no privilege. Section 10 derives browser and MCP operations from the same registry, ties a connection to app/user/team, refreshes grants per invocation and assigns mutation operation_id. Expense.create in CanExpense requires receipt:file. Test recipes finalize sample content and cannot provide production attachments. Verified MCP 2025-11-25 defines extensible _meta and server-resource retrieval through resources/read; that retrieval cannot deposit client bytes. We have not demonstrated file transfer for arbitrary chatbot hosts. Consider both a client holding a user-selected local file with Can integration and a client lacking such support. The design must never equate a path, web URL or claimed file properties with completion, expose storage secrets or endpoint selection to a model, omit final input/grant checks, invent successful execution evidence or demand repeated upload code in each app. Hold ownership, limits, quota, content validation, target checks and user/team authority constant across alternatives. Use only supplied facts, with no assumed speed or compatibility results.

handoff.instructions: Which bounded attachment interface best balances a complete receipt workflow, concise source, existing mechanisms, client availability and context consumption?

criteria.shared_host_flow: Generated MCP metadata announces a pinned Can transfer extension for a compatible host. That host reuses browser HTTPS intent, content upload and completion under the same user authorization, and supplies only the final opaque file value when calling the business operation. Owning signatures determine target/field binding instead of app-specific upload schemas. Without extension support the user receives the existing browser upload handoff. This keeps binary content outside the language-model exchange and centralizes validation, at the cost of implementing and documenting a specialized host integration; general MCP compatibility does not imply this capability.
criteria.runtime_tools: Expose common infrastructure upload tools over MCP: authorize an intent, send bounded base64 pieces and complete it. Their checks match the browser service and the final reference feeds the original mutation. Apps author no additional upload operations, and tool transport supplies the byte channel rather than separate HTTPS integration. Piece handling and access to host files are still needed; carrying encoded content through calls may greatly increase context use, and supporting MCP tools does not guarantee access to local content.
criteria.browser_only: Offer file-valued business calls only for authorized objects already completed in the browser runtime. Every new attachment requires the generated browser picker/upload first. Existing permissions stay intact, and no custom client extension or encoded-byte tools are necessary. Users incur a browser step even when their chat host could transfer content, preventing an entirely chat-based new-file task.
